proposals.before: Emperor Wenzong knew that Zhenyu was familiar with conditions in Yunnan, and therefore replaced him in the post.
proposals.after: Emperor Wenzong knew that Zhenyu was familiar with conditions in Yunnan, and therefore appointed him to replace Hengchun.
proposals.reason: Literal English reverses the object of 代之: Wenzong appointed Zhenyu to succeed Hengchun, not replaced Zhenyu.

proposals.before: Therefore before speaking of suppression he spoke of pacification, with an anguish of utter necessity; though success or failure and gain or loss cannot be foretold, apart from this there is no other good plan."
proposals.after: Therefore before speaking of suppression I spoke of pacification, with an anguish of utter necessity; though success or failure and gain or loss cannot be foretold, apart from this there is no other good plan."
proposals.reason: The memorial continues in the first person (故未言剿先言撫); literal English wrongly switches the speaker to third-person he.

proposals.before: He also reported: "Retired Vice President Huang Cong, Censor Dou Yong, and Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi were ordered to organize militia and set up a general bureau in the capital.
proposals.after: He also reported: "Retired Vice President Huang Cong, Censor Dou Yong, and Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi were ordered to organize militia and set up a general bureau in the provincial capital.
proposals.reason: 省城 is the provincial capital, not the imperial capital; the idiomatic rendering 'the capital' is misleading.

proposals.before: The capital militia now exceed ten thousand men and cost tens of thousands of taels a month—far beyond available funds.
proposals.after: The provincial-capital militia now exceed ten thousand men and cost tens of thousands of taels a month—far beyond available funds.
proposals.reason: 省練 here is the provincial-capital militia, not a force of the imperial capital.

proposals.before: Huang Cong and Dou Yong were specially dispatched personnel, beyond what your servant's strength could control; he begged an imperial decision.
proposals.after: Huang Cong and Dou Yong were specially dispatched personnel, beyond what your servant's strength could control; I begged an imperial decision.
proposals.reason: The memorial voice is first-person 請旨; literal 'he begged' wrongly shifts the speaker.

proposals.before: Zhenyu then sent Han and Hui commissioners to the capital to explain the settlement, assign residential streets, allocate abandoned property to refugees, set regulations, and send people home to their trades.
proposals.after: Zhenyu then sent Han and Hui commissioners to the provincial capital to explain the settlement, assign residential streets, allocate abandoned property to refugees, set regulations, and send people home to their trades.
proposals.reason: 省城 is the provincial capital; 'the capital' can be read as Beijing.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of 1858 the pacification was roughly in place; he moved into the capital and, with Zhang Liangji, organized suppression and pacification in western Yunnan.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of 1858 the pacification was roughly in place; he moved into the provincial capital and, with Zhang Liangji, organized suppression and pacification in western Yunnan.
proposals.reason: 入駐省城 is the provincial capital of Yunnan, not the imperial capital.

proposals.before: Liangji argued for guarding against a rebel return into Hunan—a move seen as self-serving—and the court ordered him to advance at once.
proposals.after: Liangji argued for guarding against a rebel return into Hunan, intending to concentrate on Hunan, and the court ordered him to advance at once.
proposals.reason: 意在專顧湖南 states an intent to focus on Hunan; 'self-serving' is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Transferred to Shandong before he could leave, he sent Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu to meet Jiangxi rebels from Jiujiang at Tianjiazhen; the battle was lost and Fengyu was killed; Liangji was demoted four ranks but kept his post.
proposals.after: Transferred to be governor of Shandong; before he could leave, he sent Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu to meet Jiangxi rebels from Jiujiang at Tianjiazhen; the battle was lost and Fengyu was killed; Liangji was demoted four ranks but kept his post.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names the Shandong governorship, which the idiomatic rendering drops.

proposals.before: They soon took Yancheng and raided Fan, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he cut ahead of them and defeated them at Heijiazhuang near Linqing.
proposals.after: They soon took Yuncheng and raided Fan, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he cut ahead of them and defeated them at Heijiazhuang near Linqing.
proposals.reason: The place 鄆城 is Yuncheng in Shandong, not Yancheng.

proposals.before: Soon they captured Yancheng and harassed Fan County, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he circled ahead of the bandits to intercept and defeated them at Heijiazhuang in Linqing.
proposals.after: Soon they captured Yuncheng and harassed Fan County, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he circled ahead of the bandits to intercept and defeated them at Heijiazhuang in Linqing.
proposals.reason: The place 鄆城 is Yuncheng, not Yancheng.

proposals.before: He also suppressed rebels in Yi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong, and recovered Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan in turn.
proposals.after: He also suppressed rebels in Pingyi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong, and recovered Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan in turn.
proposals.reason: Pingyi is the Yunnan county 平彝, not a bare place named Yi.

proposals.before: He also suppressed bandits in Yi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong; the prefectures and counties of Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan were recovered in succession.
proposals.after: He also suppressed bandits in Pingyi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong; the prefectures and counties of Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan were recovered in succession.
proposals.reason: 平彝 is Pingyi county, misread as Yi.

proposals.before: In the fourth year they took Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo in western Guizhou; the province was poor and funds short, hungry troops clamored for pay, and mutiny was feared at any moment.
proposals.after: In the fourth year they took Qianxi, Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo; the province was poor and funds short, hungry troops clamored for pay, and mutiny was feared at any moment.
proposals.reason: The Chinese lists 黔西 with 石阡、永寧、荔波 as captured places; 黔西 is Qianxi, not merely a regional gloss that drops the toponym.

proposals.before: Liangji pacified, controlled, and guarded against suppression and barely achieved rough stability, but many generals under his command were arrogant and obstinate, public opinion was at odds, and Academician Reader Jing Qijun memorialized to impeach him.
proposals.after: Liangji pacified, controlled, defended, and suppressed, and barely achieved rough stability, but many generals under his command were arrogant and obstinate, public opinion was at odds, and Academician Reader Jing Qijun memorialized to impeach him.
proposals.reason: 防剿 means defense and suppression, not 'guarded against suppression'.

proposals.before: In 1908 officials from Hunan and Guizhou in Beijing jointly memorialized on his public service, and he was posthumously given the temple name Huisu.
proposals.after: In 1908 officials from Hunan and Guizhou in Beijing jointly memorialized on his public service, and he was posthumously given the posthumous name Huisu.
proposals.reason: 追諡 is a posthumous name (諡), not a temple name (廟號).

proposals.before: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu, Beijing officials from Hunan and Guizhou jointly memorialized enumerating his merits among the people, and he was posthumously given the temple name Huisu.
proposals.after: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu, Beijing officials from Hunan and Guizhou jointly memorialized enumerating his merits among the people, and he was posthumously given the posthumous name Huisu.
proposals.reason: 追諡 names a posthumous title, not a temple name.

proposals.before: He memorialized: "Hunan lies in a remote corner and has never been wealthy or strong; yet former governors Zhang Liangji and Luo Zongzhang worked hard at governance and local custom, cut down bandits, and made the province a pillar of the upper Yangzi—the proof that good appointments matter is plain to see.
proposals.after: He memorialized: "Hunan lies in a remote corner and has never been wealthy or strong; yet former governors Zhang Liangji and Luo Bingzhang worked hard at governance and local custom, cut down bandits, and made the province a pillar of the upper Yangzi—the proof that good appointments matter is plain to see.
proposals.reason: 駱秉章 is Luo Bingzhang; Zongzhang misreads 秉 as 宗 and is not the established English form of this governor's name.

proposals.before: He memorialized, stating: "Hunan lies in a remote corner and has not traditionally been wealthy or strong; since former governors Zhang Liangji, Luo Zongzhang, and others applied themselves thoroughly to official governance and local customs, they were able to cut down bandits and rebels and make it stand firm as a great stronghold of the upper reaches; the effect of employing the right men has clear proof.
proposals.after: He memorialized, stating: "Hunan lies in a remote corner and has not traditionally been wealthy or strong; since former governors Zhang Liangji, Luo Bingzhang, and others applied themselves thoroughly to official governance and local customs, they were able to cut down bandits and rebels and make it stand firm as a great stronghold of the upper reaches; the effect of employing the right men has clear proof.
proposals.reason: Same name error: 駱秉章 should be Luo Bingzhang, not Luo Zongzhang.

proposals.before: The former governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou Zhang Liangji is resolute and capable; Yunnan's territory adjoins the frontier, pay and grain are not supplied, and Han-Hui enmity follows in succession; even if management were wholly excellent, it would benefit only one corner; it seems better not to assign him to a key post and let him display his strengths.
proposals.after: The former governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou Zhang Liangji is resolute and capable; Yunnan's territory adjoins the frontier, pay and grain are not supplied, and Han-Hui enmity follows in succession; even if management were wholly excellent, it would benefit only one corner; it seems better to assign him to a key post and let him display his strengths.
proposals.reason: 似不若任以要地 means it would be preferable to appoint him to a key post; the literal English inserts 'not' and reverses the recommendation.

proposals.before: He sent troops across the border against Guizhou rebels and recovered Tiancheng.
proposals.after: He sent troops across the border against Guizhou rebels and recovered Tianzhu.
proposals.reason: 天柱縣 is Tianzhu County; Tiancheng is a wrong reading of 柱.

proposals.before: He dispatched troops across the border to suppress bandits who had fled into Guizhou and recovered Tiancheng County seat.
proposals.after: He dispatched troops across the border to suppress bandits who had fled into Guizhou and recovered Tianzhu County seat.
proposals.reason: 天柱縣 is Tianzhu, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he was punished for an earlier affair in Hunan, when Intendant Hu Yong had sought permission for an imperial audience: the referral was withdrawn, an acting circuit post was voided, he was demoted one rank and transferred, and sent home.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he was punished for an earlier affair in Hunan, when Intendant Hu Yong had sought a referral for an imperial audience: the consultation document was taken back, and Hu was assigned to an acting circuit vacancy; Mao was demoted one rank, transferred, and sent home.
proposals.reason: 委署道缺 means assigning the acting circuit post, not voiding it; the punishment fell on Mao Hongbin for that handling of Hu Yong's audience request.

proposals.before: In the eighth year he and Judicial Commissioner Jiang Yizao defeated the rebels, retook Qingyuan, was restored to office, served as acting and then substantive judicial commissioner, and rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
proposals.after: In the eighth year he and Judicial Commissioner Jiang Yili defeated the rebels, retook Qingyuan, was restored to office, served as acting and then substantive judicial commissioner, and rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner.
proposals.reason: 蔣益澧 is Jiang Yili, not Jiang Yizao; the given name 益澧 is misread in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: In the eighth year, together with judicial commissioner Jiang Yizao he defeated the bandits, recovered Qingyuan, was restored to his original office, acted as judicial commissioner, was soon appointed in substantive capacity, and was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
proposals.after: In the eighth year, together with judicial commissioner Jiang Yili he defeated the bandits, recovered Qingyuan, was restored to his original office, acted as judicial commissioner, was soon appointed in substantive capacity, and was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
proposals.reason: Same misrendering of 蔣益澧 as Jiang Yizao in the literal English.

proposals.before: With Guixian pacified, he was granted an elevated honorary cap button as Qing rank insignia.
proposals.after: With Guixian pacified, he was granted the first-rank cap button.
proposals.reason: 頭品頂戴 is the first-rank court cap button; 'elevated honorary' and 'Qing rank insignia' invent wording that obscures the exact honor.

proposals.before: Kunyi was promoted to Jiangxi governor and departed; Subprefect Liu Peiyi took over his forces. Kaisong was preparing to lead the campaign at Nanning in person when the Taiping Prince Kang Wang Wang Haiyang fled into Guangdong and threatened Guangxi; the court ordered Kaisong to hold Xunzhou.
proposals.after: Kunyi was promoted to Jiangxi governor and departed; Subprefect Liu Peiyi took over his forces. Kaisong was preparing to lead the campaign at Nanning in person when the pretender Prince Kang, Wang Haiyang, fled into Guangdong and threatened Guangxi; the court ordered Kaisong to hold Xunzhou.
proposals.reason: 偽康王 marks an illegitimate Taiping princely title; the idiomatic line inserts 'Taiping' and stacks 'Kang Wang' redundantly before the personal name.

proposals.before: Commentary: Yunnan lies on a distant frontier; Han and Hui bore long-standing enmity; in an autumn when the central plains were beset with troubles, it nearly lay beyond the reach of imperial authority.
proposals.after: Commentary: Yunnan lies on a distant frontier; Han and Hui bore long-standing enmity; in a time when the central plains were beset with troubles, it nearly lay beyond the reach of imperial authority.
proposals.reason: 秋 here marks a season of crisis, not a literal autumn; rendering 多故之秋 as “in an autumn” obscures the temporal metaphor.

decisions.reason: 故以代之 takes 之 as Hengchun from the preceding sentence; Wenzong appointed Zhenyu to succeed him, and the original 'replaced him' makes Zhenyu the one removed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 文宗知振棫熟悉滇省情形，故以代之。

decisions.reason: The memorial is still in the speaker's voice after 臣 in the previous sentence; 故未言剿先言撫 has no third-person narrator, so 'he spoke' misattributes the statement.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故未言剿先言撫，有萬不得已之苦衷

decisions.reason: 設總局於省城 is the Yunnan provincial seat, not the imperial capital; bare 'the capital' can be read as Beijing.
近日省練一萬餘人 names the provincial-capital militia in Yunnan; 'the capital militia' can be taken as an imperial-capital force.
請旨定奪 is the memorialist's first-person plea; 'he begged' breaks the 臣 voice already used in 'your servant'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 非臣力所能製，請旨定奪

decisions.reason: 遣漢、回委員赴省城 sends the commissioners to Yunnan's provincial capital, not Beijing.
入駐省城 is Zhenyu's move into the Yunnan provincial capital in the eighth year, not into the imperial capital.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 八年四月，撫局粗定，入駐省城

decisions.reason: 意在專顧湖南 states Liangji's intent to concentrate on Hunan; 'self-serving' is invented and is not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 亮基疏言宜防賊回竄，意在專顧湖南

decisions.reason: 調山東巡撫 names the Shandong governorship; 'Transferred to Shandong' drops the office.
鄆城 in this Shandong campaign is Yuncheng, not Yancheng.
鄆城 is Yuncheng; Yancheng is a different toponym and a mistranslation.
平彝、安寧、緬寧、楚雄 is a list of Yunnan places; 平彝 is Pingyi, not a suppression of 'Yi'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又剿平彝、安寧、緬寧、楚雄諸匪

decisions.reason: The same list begins with the county 平彝 (Pingyi), mis-segmented in the original as 剿平 plus 彝.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又剿平彝、安寧、緬寧、楚雄諸匪

decisions.reason: 克黔西石阡、永寧、荔波 names Qianxi with Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo as places taken; 'in western Guizhou' drops 黔西 as a toponym and mislocates the others.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 四年，克黔西石阡、永寧、荔波

decisions.reason: 撫馭防剿 is pacification, control, defense, and suppression; 'guarded against suppression' reverses 防剿.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 亮基撫馭防剿，僅得粗安

decisions.reason: 追諡惠肅 is a posthumous name (諡), not a temple name (廟號).
追諡 names the posthumous title 惠肅, not a temple name.
駱秉章 is Luo Bingzhang; Zongzhang misreads 秉 as 宗.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前撫臣張亮基、駱秉章等

decisions.reason: The same personal name 駱秉章 must be Luo Bingzhang, not Luo Zongzhang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前撫臣張亮基、駱秉章等

decisions.reason: 似不若任以要地，俾展所長 recommends assigning him to a key post; inserting 'not' reverses 不若.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 似不若任以要地，俾展所長

decisions.reason: 复天柱縣城 is Tianzhu County, not Tiancheng.
天柱縣 is Tianzhu; Tiancheng misreads 柱.
繳回咨文，委署道缺 is taking back the consultation document and assigning an acting circuit vacancy, not voiding that post.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 道員胡鏞請諮引見，繳回咨文，委署道缺

decisions.reason: 蔣益澧 is Jiang Yili; Yizao is not a reading of 益澧.
The literal line has the same false English name for 蔣益澧, who is Jiang Yili.
頭品頂戴 is the first-rank cap button; 'elevated honorary' and 'Qing rank insignia' are invented and hide the exact honor.
偽康王汪海洋 is the pretender Prince Kang, Wang Haiyang; 'Taiping Prince Kang Wang Wang Haiyang' inserts Taiping and stacks 王 with the surname 汪.
中原多故之秋 is the conventional 'time of troubles'; 秋 is not the season autumn.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Luo Zongzhang was produced by misreading 秉 as 宗; the source name is 駱秉章, Luo Bingzhang.
The capture list follows the mistranslation that treated 黔西 as a regional gloss; the source names Qianxi together with Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo.
Jiang Yizao is not a reading of 蔣益澧; the restored English name is Jiang Yili.
The extracted English title stacked Taiping and Kang Wang; 偽康王 is the pretender title Prince Kang.
